title: Deployment Oscillator: temporal stability and rollback guardrails for staged rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We observe brittle canary behaviors where short-term metric fluctuations cause repeated tiny rollbacks or oscillations (traffic rapidly moves up/down across steps), sometimes triggering flapping incidents and noisy alerts. This becomes visible during load bursts and when multiple rollouts overlap in the same capacity pool.

Goal: Implement an orchestration layer — "Deployment Oscillator" — that enforces temporal stability and multi-signal guardrails for staged rollouts. The engine should: enforce minimum dwell time per step; apply confidence windows and decay for noisy metrics; support jittered step schedules to avoid synchronized pushes; provide shadow/observe-only toggles for initial validation; and incorporate auto-rollback rules with safe cool-down and manual override hooks.

Key constraints and trade-offs:
- Latency-sensitive traffic requires short dwell times; longer dwell reduces false positives but increases rollout duration. We will make dwell time configurable per project/team with sane defaults.
- Aggregating signals (latency p95, error spike, downstream backpressure, cost anomalies) reduces single-signal false alarms but increases computation/metric fan-in. We will compute aggregated health scores server-side and expose decomposed reasons.
- Jittering step transitions reduces global synchronization risk but complicates deterministic sequencing for audits; we will log and record actual transition timestamps.
- Auto-rollback should prefer conservative actions (step back, pause) before full rollback.

High-level design summary: a declarative rollout policy schema (weights, min_dwell, max_dwell, confidence_thresholds, decay_window, jitter_percentage, shadow_mode) plus a runtime policy evaluator that samples traffic according to weights, maintains a per-rollout health ledger, and executes actions (advance, pause, step-back, rollback) via the existing rollout API. The evaluator will emit detailed audit events and an observability dashboard tile for each rollout instance.
acceptance_criteria: Declarative rollout policy schema v1 defined and stored in rollout-configs (fields: initial_weights, step_schedule, min_dwell_secs, max_dwell_secs, confidence_thresholds, decay_window_secs, jitter_pct, shadow_mode)
Runtime evaluator implements min_dwell enforcement and prevents step transitions before configured dwell time unless override is explicitly requested
Health aggregator computes a single health score from at least 3 signals (p95_latency, error_rate, infra_retries) and exposes signal breakdown in logs and UI
A configurable jitter mechanism applies random +/- jitter_pct to scheduled transition times to reduce synchronized rollouts
Auto-rollback rules: when aggregated health < critical_threshold for persist_window_secs, the engine performs step-back or full rollback per policy; actions are auditable and reversible
Shadow mode toggles traffic duplication without affecting primary weights and records divergence metrics in the console
End-to-end integration tests and unit tests cover dwell enforcement, jitter, health aggregation, and rollback actions
Dashboard tile + per-rollout event stream implemented to surface rollouts with their timeline and reason codes
tasks: Design doc: write detailed policy schema and state machine (Confluence: /r/rd/policies/deployment-oscillator) - high priority
Metric contract: define inputs and normalization rules for p95_latency, error_rate, infra_retries (SLA team sync)
Implement policy parser and validation in rollout service (backend) - create feature branch ENG-55321/deployment-oscillator
Implement evaluator: dwell timer, jitter scheduler, health aggregator, action executor; add audit events
Add UI widgets: rollout timeline, reason codes, manual override controls (Console PR)
E2E tests: simulate metric noise and concurrent rollouts, verify no oscillation and correct rollback behavior
Performance review: ensure evaluator overhead < 2% of request path and aggregator scales with number of concurrent rollouts
Security review and KMS checks (if rollout config contains encrypted fields)
